entries.title: Psalms 55:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Voice - Their clamours and threats, and slanders. Cast - They lay many crimes to my charge.

entries.title: Psalms 55:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The terrors - Deadly terrors; such as seize upon men in the agonies of death.

entries.title: Psalms 55:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Tempest - From the force and fury of mine enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 55:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Destroy - Destroy them by dividing. Tongues - Their speech, as thou didst at Babel, Gen 11:9, their votes, and opinions, and counsels. Which was eminently done among Absalom's followers, 2Sam 17:23. Strife - Injustice and fraud, oppression and contention rule here, instead of that public justice and peace which I established. City - In Jerusalem; which in Absalom's time was a sink of all sins.

entries.title: Psalms 55:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They - Violence and strife. Go about - Do encompass it, as it were a garrison. Walls - In the outward parts, as also in the very midst of it. So that all parts were horribly corrupted.

entries.title: Psalms 55:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Streets - The places of buying and selling, and of public commerce.

entries.title: Psalms 55:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hated - With a manifest or old hatred.

entries.title: Psalms 55:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Equal - Not in power, but in reputation, for wisdom, and influence upon my people. Guide - Whose counsel I highly prized, and constantly followed. All which agrees to Achitophel.

entries.title: Psalms 55:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Them - All such as pretend to religion, and have manifestly apostatized both from the profession and practice of it. The grave - Cut off by a sudden and violent death. Among them - Heb. in their inwards. Wickedness is deeply rooted in their hearts.

entries.title: Psalms 55:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Evening, &100. - The three stated times of prayer among the Jews.

entries.title: Psalms 55:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He hath - He speaks of a future deliverance, as a thing done, because of the certainty of it. He hath restored me to my former peace and tranquility. For - For there were more with me than against me; even the holy angels whom God employed to defend and deliver me.

entries.title: Psalms 55:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hear - My prayers. Eternity - Who is eternal, and therefore unchangeable, and almighty. Because - They meet with no crosses nor disappointments. Therefore - Their success makes them go on securely, without any regard to God, or dread of his judgments.

entries.title: Psalms 55:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Burden - All thy crosses, and cares, and fears, lay them upon the Almighty, by faith and prayer. He directs this speech to his own soul, and to all good men in like circumstances. Suffer - As he doth wicked men. Tho' he may for a season suffer them to be shaken, yet not to be overwhelmed.

entries.title: Psalms 55:23–56:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Them - The wicked. Not live - But shall be cut off by an untimely and violent death. Trust in thee - And in this confidence I will quietly wait for deliverance.
